pop: 63,000 (Highland Council settlement estimate; ~70,000 in greater urban area)
tagline: Capital of the Highlands, where the River Ness meets the sea
card: Contactless and card payment are the norm almost everywhere, including buses and small cafes; cash is rarely needed but ATMs are widely available
rides: Local private-hire firms (Uber does not operate in Inverness)

taxi.color: No single livery — mix of black cabs and private-hire saloons/estates
taxi.fareNote: Fixed fares commonly quoted for the airport (~£25/$32) and Loch Ness day trips; book by phone as street hailing is limited

emergency.medical: 999 for emergencies, 111 for NHS non-emergency advice; Raigmore Hospital is the main hospital
emergency.note: 112 also reaches emergency services (EU-standard number, works throughout the UK)

visit: Old Town wynds and Victorian Market
Leakey's Bookshop in a converted church
River Ness walk to the Ness Islands
Clava Cairns Bronze Age standing stones
Drumnadrochit and the Loch Ness Centre
Urquhart Castle ruins on Loch Ness
Craft beer tasting at Uilebheist Distillery & Brewery
walk: Compact, walkable city centre — most sights are within a 15-20 minute walk of each other, linked by footbridges over the River Ness and the pedestrian paths of the Ness Islands

safety.safety: Very safe overall — Inverness and the Highlands consistently rank among the lowest-crime areas in the UK
safety.crime: Violent crime is rare; petty theft is uncommon but standard caution is sensible in the city centre late at night around pubs on weekends

hood_landmark.Merkinch: Merkinch Local Nature Reserve & Carnarc Point
hood_landmark.Ballifeary: Ness Islands footbridges & Eden Court Theatre

hood_desc: The compact heart of Inverness on the east bank of the River Ness, packed with the castle, cathedral, Victorian Market arcades, and most restaurants, pubs and shops within easy walking distance.

A hillside Victorian and Edwardian conservation area just south of the centre, historically linked to the old castle lands, now a quiet, affluent residential neighborhood centred on a small crossroads of cafes and pubs.
A traditionally working-class district on a former island between the Caledonian Canal and the River Ness, with a strong community identity, riverside walks, and the Merkinch Local Nature Reserve.
A leafy riverside residential area on the west bank near the Ness Islands, home to Eden Court Theatre and several of the city's guesthouses in converted Victorian villas.
A hillside residential suburb south of the centre with woodland walks, mostly modern housing, and a handful of guesthouses popular with drivers arriving via the A9.

transit.sys: Stagecoach Highlands city and regional buses (no rail metro or tram)
transit.hours: Roughly 06:00-23:30 on main routes, with a reduced Sunday timetable
transit.pay: Contactless card/phone tap, the Stagecoach app, or cash on board
transit.map: Stagecoach Highlands Inverness zone map covers the city and surrounding villages such as Culloden, Smithton and the airport
transit.note: The city centre is small enough to walk entirely; buses are mainly useful for outlying suburbs, the airport, and day trips to Loch Ness or Culloden

transport.air: Inverness Airport (INV) has direct flights from London (Heathrow, Gatwick, Luton), Amsterdam, Dublin, Belfast and other UK/European cities
transport.train: ScotRail direct trains from Edinburgh (~3.5 hrs), Glasgow (~3.25 hrs) and Aberdeen (~2 hrs); the Caledonian Sleeper runs overnight from London Euston
transport.bus: Scottish Citylink and Megabus coaches connect Inverness Bus Station with Edinburgh, Glasgow, Aberdeen and other Scottish cities
transport.ferry: No direct ferry into Inverness; nearest ferry terminals are Ullapool (to Stornoway, Isle of Lewis) and Scrabster (to Orkney), each about a 1-2 hour drive
transport.car: A9 from Perth/Edinburgh in the south, A96 from Aberdeen, A82 from Fort William and Glasgow along Loch Ness

airport.name: Inverness Airport
airport.distance: 9 miles (15 km) northeast of the city centre, at Dalcross
airport.transport: Stagecoach service 11/11A/11B, about 40 minutes, roughly $6 (£5); taxi about 20 minutes, roughly $32 (£25) for up to 4 passengers

net.m: Good 4G/5G coverage in Inverness itself; coverage gets patchy in rural Highland glens
net.w: Widely available in cafes, pubs, hotels and the public library
net.gb: Around $15-20 for a 15-20GB pay-as-you-go SIM bundle
net.fwn: Free wifi is standard with a purchase at cafes like Velocity Cafe and Black Isle Bar, plus free access at Inverness Public Library
net.ap: Buy a pay-as-you-go SIM (EE, Three or Vodafone) at a supermarket or the airport on arrival, or set up an eSIM before the trip

tip.s: Not obligatory for taxis or general services; rounding up or adding a small amount for good service is appreciated but not expected
tip.r: 10-12% for table service if not already added; always check the bill for an included 'service charge' before tipping again

pop: 8,900 (combined Windermere & Bowness-on-Windermere civil parish, 2021 census; Windermere town alone: 4,826)
tagline: England's largest lake, one grand fell-top view at a time
card: Widely accepted, contactless is standard in shops, cafes, pubs, and even on Windermere Lake Cruises boats. Carry a little cash for rural B&Bs, market stalls, or small fell-side tea rooms.
rides: Local pre-booked taxi firms (Lakes Taxis, Applecabs, Fellrunner Taxis)
Uber/Bolt do not operate in the Lake District

taxi.color: No standard livery, mostly private saloons and estate cars
taxi.fareNote: Most journeys are phone- or app-pre-booked rather than hailed on the street; agree a fixed price for longer runs (e.g., to Kendal or the airport).

emergency.medical: 999 for emergencies; nearest A&E is Westmorland General Hospital, Kendal (about 9 miles away)
emergency.note: Mountain Rescue (Kendal MRT / Langdale-Ambleside MRT) responds to fell and hiking incidents — always dial 999 and ask for Police then Mountain Rescue.

visit: Windermere Jetty Museum of Boats, Steam & Stories
Cross-lake ferry from Ferry Nab to Far Sawrey
Hill Top (Beatrix Potter's farmhouse, Near Sawrey)
Orrest Head viewpoint walk from Windermere town
Brockhole – The Lake District Visitor Centre
Day trip to Ambleside: Bridge House and Stock Ghyll Force waterfall
Grasmere village and Dove Cottage (Wordsworth's home)
walk: Bowness-on-Windermere is compact and pedestrian-friendly along the bay, and it connects to Windermere town by a signed 25-30 minute uphill footpath. Beyond the two centers, pavements thin out fast on rural lanes, so sturdy shoes are needed for fell walks, and the terrain is genuinely hilly.

safety.safety: Very safe; Cumbria consistently has one of the lowest crime rates in England and Windermere/Bowness feel comfortable to walk after dark.
safety.crime: Petty theft is the main risk — car break-ins at remote fell-side car parks and unattended bags at busy lake piers in summer. Violent crime is rare. Fell/hiking mishaps are a bigger practical safety concern than crime.

hood_landmark.Bowness-on-Windermere: Bowness Bay piers and Windermere Lake Cruises terminal
hood_landmark.Windermere town: Orrest Head viewpoint and the 1847 railway station
hood_landmark.Storrs / Storrs Park: Storrs Hall and Storrs Temple on the lakeshore

hood_desc: The bustling lakeside hub with the cruise piers, ice cream stalls, pubs and The World of Beatrix Potter — the tourist heart of Windermere.
The quieter hilltop town that grew up around the 1847 railway terminus, with independent shops and cafes and an easy walk up to the classic fell-top view at Orrest Head.
A largely unspoiled Lakeland farming village of slate-roofed cottages strung along a valley just north of Windermere, home to the historic Townend farmhouse.
A lively outdoor-adventure town at the lake's northern tip, packed with hiking-gear shops, cafes and waterfall walks, a short bus or boat ride from Bowness.
A genteel, wooded stretch of lakeshore south of Bowness lined with grand Victorian hotels and historic estates, good for a quiet lakeside stroll away from the crowds.

transit.sys: Windermere Lake Cruises ferry network plus Stagecoach Cumbria buses; no local rail beyond the Windermere branch-line terminus
transit.hours: Cruises run roughly 9:45am–5:30pm; buses generally run about 7am–11pm
transit.pay: Buses: tap card or cash on board; cruises: buy at the pier kiosk or online. Day passes exist for both.
transit.map: Route maps posted at Windermere Lake Cruises piers and on the Stagecoach Cumbria and Traveline websites
transit.note: A separate small car-and-passenger chain ferry crosses the lake year-round at Ferry Nab to Far Sawrey — handy for reaching Hill Top and Hawkshead without driving around the lake.

transport.air: Nearest airport is Manchester Airport (MAN), about 90 miles away; Liverpool John Lennon and Newcastle are secondary options.
transport.train: Windermere railway station is the terminus of a branch line with roughly hourly trains to/from Manchester Airport and Manchester Piccadilly (about 2 hours); London Euston connects via Oxenholme on the West Coast Main Line in about 3.5–4 hours.
transport.bus: National Express coaches link major UK cities to Kendal/Windermere; local Stagecoach Cumbria buses connect Windermere/Bowness with Ambleside, Grasmere, Kendal and the wider national park.
transport.ferry: No international ferry service; Windermere Lake Cruises and the small Ferry Nab car ferry handle only on-lake, local travel.
transport.car: Via the M6 (Junction 36) then the A591, about 2.5–3 hours from Manchester or Liverpool. Parking in central Bowness and Windermere is limited and expensive in peak season.

airport.name: Manchester Airport
airport.distance: About 90 miles / 145 km (roughly 2–2.5 hours by train or car)
airport.transport: Direct or one-change trains run from Manchester Airport station to Windermere roughly hourly (~2 hours); pre-booked private transfers cost roughly $180–250 one-way and take about 2 hours

net.m: 4G is generally reliable in the Bowness and Windermere town centers but drops out frequently on fells, in valleys, and around villages like Troutbeck; 5G coverage is limited.
net.w: Free Wi-Fi is common in cafes, pubs and hotels in town; coverage is patchier at rural attractions and on the trails.
net.gb: About $15–25 for a 15–20GB tourist SIM or eSIM
net.fwn: Most cafes, hotels and the Brockhole National Park Visitor Centre offer free Wi-Fi to customers
net.ap: SIM cards available at Manchester Airport and phone shops in Windermere/Ambleside; eSIMs can be activated before arrival

tip.s: Tipping is not obligatory anywhere in the UK. Rounding up a taxi fare or leaving small change at a cafe is appreciated but not expected.
tip.r: In restaurants and pubs with table service, 10–12.5% is typical if a service charge isn't already added to the bill.

pop: ~1.5 million (Zhangjiajie prefecture-level city, spanning Yongding District, Wulingyuan District, Cili County and Sangzhi County)
tagline: Where the sandstone pillars of Avatar's Pandora rise straight out of the mist
card: Cash and mobile QR payments (Alipay, WeChat Pay) dominate almost every transaction, from noodle stalls to scenic-area ticket booths; foreign Visa/Mastercard are accepted only at large international hotels like the InterContinental or Pullman. Set up Alipay's Tour Pass or link a foreign card to WeChat Pay before arrival, and carry some cash as backup.

taxi.fareNote: About ¥1.8–2/km after the first 2–3 km; drivers rarely speak English so have your destination written in Chinese characters or use Didi's in-app translation

emergency.note: Fire is 119. Tourist police booths are stationed at the entrances of Zhangjiajie National Forest Park and Tianmen Mountain; hotel front desks are often the fastest way to get help translated.

religion: Tujia and Miao ethnic folk traditions
visit: Tianmen Mountain cable car ride from downtown
Wulingyuan old town / Suoxiyu village stroll
walk: Not a stroll-around city — Zhangjiajie is a hiking and cable-car destination built into vertical sandstone-pillar terrain. Expect thousands of stone steps, steep switchback trails, and long walkways through the national forest park; shuttle buses, cable cars, and the Bailong Elevator handle the big elevation changes. Downtown Yongding District is flat and walkable.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers by international standards; violent crime against tourists is extremely rare. The main risks are trail-related — steep drop-offs, slick stone steps in rain or fog, and getting lost off marked paths.
safety.crime: Petty theft is uncommon but not unheard of at peak-season entrances; standard vigilance with valuables is enough. Overcharging by unlicensed tour touts and off-app taxi drivers is the more common annoyance.

hood_landmark.Yongding District (Downtown Zhangjiajie): Tianmen Mountain cable car base station
hood_landmark.Wulingyuan District: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park & Golden Whip Stream

hood_desc: The prefecture's urban core, with the train and long-distance bus stations, the bulk of mid-range hotels, restaurants, and the world's longest cable car line climbing straight out of the city to Tianmen Mountain.
The gateway town to the core UNESCO scenic area, packed with guesthouses just outside the National Forest Park gate; this is the launch point for Golden Whip Stream and the Bailong Elevator.
A quieter valley within Wulingyuan Scenic Area centered on Baofeng Lake's jade-green water and the pillar-lined Ten-Mile Gallery, popular for an easier-paced day away from the busiest trails.
Home to the park's most photographed pillar formations, including the cliffs said to have inspired the floating Hallelujah Mountains of Pandora in Avatar.
An adventure-tourism hub built around the record-breaking glass bridge spanning the Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon, with zip-lining and bungee add-ons for thrill-seekers.

transit.sys: No metro or tram; city buses run downtown, and mandatory eco-friendly shuttle buses (fare included in the park ticket) move visitors between trailheads inside Zhangjiajie National Forest Park and Wulingyuan Scenic Area.
transit.hours: City buses roughly 6:30am–7pm; park shuttles run from park opening (~7am) to around 6pm, earlier in winter
transit.pay: Cash, Alipay, or WeChat Pay on city buses; scenic-area shuttles are covered by your entrance ticket
transit.map: Amap (Gaode Ditu) or Baidu Maps for navigation; free paper trail maps handed out at park entrance gates
transit.note: Cable cars, the Bailong Elevator, and the Tianmen Mountain cable car all require separate paid tickets on top of park admission.

transport.air: Zhangjiajie Hehua International Airport (DYG) has direct flights from Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu, Xi'an, and other major Chinese hubs, plus seasonal charters from a handful of Southeast Asian cities.
transport.train: Zhangjiajie West high-speed rail station puts Changsha about 2 hours away and links onward to the national high-speed network; the older Zhangjiajie railway station handles slower conventional trains.
transport.bus: Long-distance coaches connect Zhangjiajie's bus stations to Changsha, Fenghuang Ancient Town, and other Hunan destinations.
transport.ferry: None — Zhangjiajie is deep inland in mountainous northwestern Hunan with no navigable ferry routes.
transport.car: Self-driving is possible via the Changsha–Zhangjiajie and Zhangjiajie–Jishou expressways, but requires a Chinese driving permit; mountain roads within the scenic areas are best left to shuttle buses or a hired driver.

airport.name: Zhangjiajie Hehua International Airport
airport.distance: ~7 miles (11 km) south of downtown Zhangjiajie (Yongding District)
airport.transport: Taxi ~$8–12 (20–25 min); airport shuttle bus to city center for around $1.50; no direct rail link

net.m: China Mobile, China Unicom, and China Telecom all sell prepaid tourist SIMs with data at the airport and downtown shops; eSIM options from international providers also work well
net.w: Free Wi-Fi is common in hotels and many cafes downtown, but weaker to nonexistent deep inside the scenic parks
net.ops: China Mobile, China Unicom, China Telecom
net.gb: $3–6 per GB on a prepaid tourist SIM
net.fwn: Google, Gmail, Maps, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and most Western news sites are blocked; install a reliable VPN before you arrive
net.ap: Cell signal is generally solid even on cable cars and ridgelines, though it can drop in valley trails and cave sections like Tianmen Cave

tip.s: Tipping is not customary anywhere in China, including for taxi drivers, hotel staff, or tour guides; attempting to tip can even cause confusion.
tip.r: Restaurants do not expect tips and never add a service charge at local eateries; only some high-end international hotel restaurants may quietly include one.

tagline: Powder-white sand, turquoise water, and a sunset over Willy's Rock
card: Widely accepted at hotels, resorts, dive shops and larger restaurants; small beachfront eateries, sari-sari stores, tricycles and market stalls are cash-only — keep PHP on hand for daily spending.

taxi.fare: ₱25-50 shared per person along the main road; ₱150-300 chartered
taxi.fareNote: Boracay banned private cars and vans on the main road in 2018 — official blue/white e-trikes and tricycles are the only motorized transport on the island itself; agree on price before boarding if unmetered.

emergency.police: 911 (national emergency line) or Boracay Police Station (Station 2): (036) 288-3061
emergency.medical: 911 or Boracay Community Hospital / Ciriaco B. Tirol Memorial District Hospital in Kalibo for serious cases
emergency.note: Serious trauma cases are typically airlifted or ferried to Kalibo or Iloilo City; Department of Tourism hotline is 1-386 (domestic) for tourist assistance.

visit: Arrive via Caticlan jetty port, check in at your Station
Walk White Beach at sunset near Willy's Rock (Station 1)
Island-hopping tour: Crystal Cove Island, Crocodile Island, Magic Island snorkeling stop
Kitesurfing or windsurfing lesson at Bulabog Beach
Spa treatment or massage on the beach
Ariel's Point cliff-jumping and BBQ boat trip (seasonal)
Sunrise hike or ATV ride to Mt. Luho viewpoint
Puka Shell Beach for a quieter swim and fresh buko shake
Motag Living Museum and Boracay handicraft shopping at D'Mall before departure
walk: White Beach's beachfront path and Station 2's D'Mall are extremely walkable and barefoot-friendly; the island is long and narrow (~7km) so tricycles or e-trikes are used for cross-island trips, especially in midday heat.

safety.safety: Generally very safe for solo travelers, including women
safety.crime: Violent crime against tourists is rare; petty theft (unattended bags/phones on the beach, occasional overcharging by unlicensed tricycles) is the main risk — use officially marked tricycles and secure valuables.

hood_landmark.Diniwid Beach: Hidden cove cliffside footpath from Station 1

hood_desc: Boracay's most scenic and upscale stretch of White Beach, home to Willy's Rock grotto, wide soft sand and higher-end resorts, with a quieter, more relaxed vibe than Station 2.

The bustling heart of the island, anchored by D'Mall's maze of restaurants, bars, souvenir shops and travel agencies; loud, crowded and walkable, with the widest range of budgets and the liveliest nightlife strip.
The narrower, quieter southern end of White Beach popular with backpackers and budget travelers, with fewer crowds and a more local, laid-back feel.

The island's east-coast windward beach, the Philippines' top kitesurfing and windsurfing spot thanks to steady onshore winds; rockier and not swimmable at low tide but full of watersports schools and chill beach bars.

A small, secluded cove just north of Station 1 reached by a cliffside footpath, known for calmer water, a rustic laid-back crowd, and some of the island's best sunset viewing away from the main strip.

transit.sys: E-trikes and tricycles on the single main road; pump boats (bangkas) for inter-island and mainland transfers
transit.hours: E-trikes run roughly 5am-midnight; jetty boats to Caticlan operate about 5am-8pm regularly, with limited service later
transit.pay: Cash (PHP) paid directly to the driver or boatman; agree on fare before boarding for unmetered chartered trips
transit.map: No formal transit map — the island has one main beachfront path (White Beach) and one inland concrete road (Boracay Main Road) running its length
transit.note: Private cars and vans have been banned from the main road since a 2018 island rehabilitation closure; only permitted e-trikes, tricycles and bicycles operate on-island.

transport.air: Fly into Godofredo P. Ramos Airport (Caticlan, code MPH), a 10-min tricycle ride plus 15-min boat from the island; Kalibo International Airport (KLO) is a further ~1.5-2 hr van/bus ride to Caticlan and serves more international carriers.
transport.train: No rail service anywhere on Panay island; nearest rail options are in Manila.
transport.bus: Overnight buses (e.g. Ceres Bus Lines) run from Manila to Caticlan (~12-14 hrs) via the Nabas/RORO ferry route, then a short boat crossing to Boracay.
transport.ferry: Frequent pump boats cross the Tabon Strait between Caticlan Jetty Port and Boracay's Cagban or Tambisaan jetty in 10-15 minutes, roughly every 30-60 minutes.
transport.car: No private car rentals are usable on Boracay itself; visitors drive/rent only for reaching Caticlan or Kalibo on Panay island, then leave the vehicle before the boat crossing.

airport.name: Godofredo P. Ramos Airport (Caticlan)
airport.distance: ~2km from Boracay Island: 10-min tricycle to Caticlan Jetty Port + 15-min boat crossing + short tricycle to your hotel
airport.transport: ₱500-700 DIY door-to-door via tricycle+terminal fee+environmental fee+boat+tricycle; ₱950-1,050 for a pre-booked private transfer; alt airport Kalibo (KLO), ~1.5-2 hr drive to Caticlan Jetty Port

net.m: Good 4G/5G coverage across the island from Globe and Smart; speeds can slow during peak season crowds
net.w: Free wifi is common in hotels, resorts and cafes but can be slow/unreliable — many travelers rely on mobile data instead
net.gb: Prepaid tourist SIM with ~5-8GB data runs about ₱500-800 (~$8-13)
net.fwn: Networks are usually named after the establishment (e.g. hotel/resort wifi), password given at check-in or on menus
net.ap: SIM cards sold at both airports and at kiosks/malls along D'Mall in Station 2

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated — round up or leave ₱50-100 for hotel staff, boatmen and tour guides for good service
tip.r: A 10% service charge is often already added to the bill at resorts/restaurants; if not, 10% is a welcome tip for good service

tagline: Limestone cliffs, hidden lagoons, and the edge of Bacuit Bay
card: Cash (PHP) is essential — many small resorts, tour boats, and eateries are cash-only. Larger hotels and some restaurants take cards (often with a 3-5% surcharge). ATMs exist in El Nido town and at Lio but occasionally run out of cash, especially on weekends.

taxi.color: No metered taxis — El Nido runs on open-air tricycles (motorbike with sidecar), usually white or brightly painted
taxi.fare: ₱50-150 (~$1-3) for short hops within town or to Corong-Corong
taxi.fareNote: Fares are negotiated upfront, not metered; a tricycle to Nacpan Beach (round trip) runs about ₱600-800 (~$10-14)

emergency.police: 911 (national emergency hotline); El Nido Municipal Police Station in Poblacion
emergency.medical: El Nido has a small district hospital/rural health unit for minor issues; serious cases are transferred to Ospital ng Palawan or Palawan Adventist Hospital in Puerto Princesa (~5 hrs by road)
emergency.note: DOT Tourist Assistance hotline: 1343 (domestic); get travel insurance with medevac coverage given the distance to major hospitals

visit: Arrive via El Nido/Lio Airport (ENI) or van transfer from Puerto Princesa
Check in around El Nido Town/Poblacion or Corong-Corong
Stroll the town pier and Calle Hama/Real Street
Sunset at Corong-Corong Beach or a Las Cabanas floating bar
Island Hopping Tour A: Big Lagoon, Small Lagoon (Secret Lagoon), 7 Commando Beach, Shimizu Island, Payong-Payong Island
Evening drinks at a beach bar in town
Island Hopping Tour C: Hidden Beach, Secret Beach, Helicopter Island, Matinloc Shrine, Talisay Beach
Sunset from a rooftop bar or Art Cafe in town
Day trip to Nacpan Beach and Calitang (Twin Beach)
Beach hammocks, coconut stands, and swimming
Optional Taraw Peak/Taraw Cliff sunrise or sunset hike above town
walk: El Nido Town/Poblacion itself is compact and walkable corner to corner in 10-15 minutes, but Corong-Corong, Lio, Las Cabanas, and Nacpan require a tricycle, scooter, or van — roads outside the center are often unpaved and unlit at night.

safety.safety: Generally very safe for solo travelers, including women; locals are used to independent tourists and tour groups create built-in social safety
safety.crime: Low violent crime; petty theft of unattended valuables on beaches and occasional tour/overcharging scams are the main risks; roads outside town have no streetlights after dark

hood_landmark.El Nido Town / Poblacion: El Nido Pier and Taraw Cliff (Taraw Peak) viewpoint
hood_landmark.Lio Beach: Lio Tourism Estate and Art Park

hood_desc: The bustling town center where every tour boat departs — narrow lanes packed with dive shops, souvenir stalls, budget guesthouses, and the restaurant strip along Calle Hama and Real Street.
A quieter beachfront barangay just south of town with a long sandy stretch, boutique resorts, and some of the best unobstructed sunset views over Bacuit Bay.
A postcard cove south of Corong-Corong known for its floating sunset bar, calm swimming waters, and views of Cadlao Island — popular for a golden-hour drink.
A master-planned tourism estate by the airport with manicured paths, an outdoor art park, upscale cafes, and a long white-sand beach — a polished contrast to the town.
A remote, still-developing double beach about 40 minutes north of town, framed by coconut palms and largely free of the crowds found closer to El Nido proper.

transit.sys: No formal public transit — tricycles, habal-habal motorbikes, and shared/private vans cover local trips; boats (bangkas) handle inter-island and beach transport
transit.hours: Roughly 6am-10pm for tricycles/vans; island-hopping boats run 9am-5pm
transit.pay: Cash only, fares negotiated on the spot
transit.map: No formal transit map — distances are short and drivers/boatmen know all beaches and resorts by name
transit.note: Renting a scooter (~₱500-600/day) is popular for reaching Nacpan and Las Cabanas independently

transport.air: El Nido/Lio Airport (ENI) has direct flights from Manila via AirSWIFT (~2h20m-2h50m); most travelers instead fly into Puerto Princesa (PPS), which has far more flights
transport.train: No rail service anywhere in Palawan
transport.bus: No direct long-distance bus from Manila; shared vans/shuttles run the 5-5.5 hour Puerto Princesa to El Nido route
transport.ferry: Weekly Manila-Coron-Puerto Princesa passenger ferries; no scheduled ferry directly serves El Nido
transport.car: Rental scooters/motorbikes and private vans are available in town; roads to Nacpan and San Vicente are partly unpaved and best driven in daylight

airport.name: El Nido Airport (Lio Airport)
airport.distance: ~4 km / 10 min from El Nido town center, adjacent to Lio Beach
airport.transport: Puerto Princesa International Airport (PPS) is the main gateway, followed by a 5-5.5 hr van transfer (~$12-14)

net.m: Globe and Smart are the two main mobile carriers; DITO has limited coverage
net.w: Hotel/resort wifi is common but often slow and unreliable, especially in wet season or on outer islands
net.gb: ₱500-800 (~$9-14) for a ~15-20GB prepaid data pack valid 30 days
net.fwn: Free wifi at most cafes, restaurants, and hotels, though speeds vary widely by location
net.ap: Puerto Princesa and Manila airports sell tourist SIMs; El Nido town has several small phone-load/SIM shops

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for tricycle drivers, tour guides, and boat crews — round up or add ₱50-100 per person for a full-day tour
tip.r: A 10% service charge is often already included at resorts and larger restaurants; where it isn't, 10% is a generous, appreciated tip

tagline: Limestone cliffs, hidden lagoons, and sunken warships in the Calamian Islands
card: Cash is essential — tricycles, market stalls, small eateries, and island-hopping boat crews are cash-only. Larger hotels, dive shops, and a few restaurants along the waterfront accept cards (often with a 3-5% surcharge). Only a handful of ATMs exist in town and they occasionally run out of cash.

taxi.color: open-air motorized tricycles (no metered taxis exist)
taxi.fareNote: Fares are flat-rate or negotiated up front, not metered; a full tricycle charter runs roughly ₱150-300/hour, and habal-habal rides to outlying beaches cost ₱100-300

emergency.police: 911 (national emergency hotline); Coron Municipal Police Station
emergency.medical: Coron District Hospital; Maria Elena Hospital also serves the town
emergency.note: The nearest hyperbaric recompression chamber is in Puerto Princesa or Manila; for serious trauma, medevac to Manila or Cebu is often required

visit: Mt. Tapyas sunset hike (721 steps, panoramic view of Coron Bay)
Tour A: Kayangan Lake (voted Asia's cleanest lake)
CYC Beach and Malawig Bay island hopping
Tour D/wreck diving: Japanese WWII shipwrecks (Akitsushima, Okikawa Maru, Kogyo Maru)
Relax at a Marina waterfront café
Coron Town food crawl and sunset drinks
walk: Coron Town Proper (Poblacion) is compact and walkable end to end in about 15-20 minutes, with the market, pier, and Mt. Tapyas staircase all in range. Nearly everything outside downtown — the lakes, lagoons, wrecks, and outer beaches — requires a boat tour or tricycle/habal-habal ride.

safety.safety: Generally safe for solo travelers, including women traveling alone; the town is small, friendly, and used to tourists
safety.crime: Violent crime is rare; the main risks are overpriced or unlicensed tour operators, tricycle drivers overcharging tourists, and opportunistic theft of phones/bags left unattended. Always confirm tour operators are DOT-accredited.

hood_desc: The commercial heart of Coron — Real Street and the public market are lined with travel agencies, dive shops, souvenir stalls, and the base of the Mt. Tapyas staircase. Most budget guesthouses and the bulk of restaurants are here.
The strip along Coron Bay near the municipal pier where island-hopping bangkas depart each morning; by night it turns into the town's bar and restaurant row, with rooftop spots overlooking the water.

A quieter, more residential stretch northeast of downtown fronting a calm swimming beach, popular with backpackers and long-stay divers who want a short tricycle ride from the action rather than being in the middle of it.
A mixed residential-tourism barangay south of downtown near the jungle path to Maquinit Hot Spring, with mid-range resorts set back from the noise of the town center.

The limestone karst island across the bay, ancestral domain of the Tagbanwa people, home to Kayangan Lake, Barracuda Lake and Twin Lagoon — visited on day tours rather than stayed in, though a few private-island luxury resorts sit just offshore.
lodging: Two Seasons Coron Island Resort & Spa

transit.sys: Tricycles and habal-habal motorbikes for town/land routes; bangka (outrigger boats) for island-hopping and inter-island transfers
transit.hours: Tricycles run roughly 6am-10pm; island-hopping boats depart 8-9am and return by 4-5pm
transit.pay: Cash (PHP) only, fares are negotiated or flat-rate
transit.map: No formal transit map exists; the town is small enough that any tricycle driver or hotel staff can direct you
transit.note: There is no public bus, jeepney, or ride-hailing app network in Coron — tricycles, habal-habal, and chartered boats are the only options, and Grab does not operate here

transport.air: Fly into Francisco B. Reyes Airport (USU) on Busuanga Island via AirSWIFT, Cebgo/PAL Express, or Sunlight Air — about 1 hour from Manila and under 1.5 hours from Cebu
transport.train: No rail service anywhere in Palawan
transport.bus: No direct long-distance bus reaches Coron; local vans and multicabs shuttle between the airport and town, and rough-road van/habal-habal trips connect to El Nido (5-6 hours)
transport.ferry: 2GO Travel runs a weekly passenger ferry between Manila and Coron (roughly 13-15 hours); smaller RORO and outrigger routes connect Coron to Puerto Princesa, El Nido, and Culion
transport.car: Self-drive rentals are uncommon; most visitors hire a habal-habal, tricycle, or private van with driver for overland trips

airport.name: Francisco B. Reyes Airport (Busuanga Airport)
airport.distance: ~25 km / 40-50 minutes from Coron town proper by shared van or private transfer
airport.transport: Airport shuttle vans (~₱400-600 per person) meet every flight; private transfers and hotel pickups also available; no public bus service

net.m: Globe, Smart, and DITO all have coverage in Coron town, but signal drops out quickly on the water and around outer islands and lakes
net.w: Most hotels, hostels, and cafés offer free wifi, though speeds are often slow and inconsistent given the island's limited bandwidth
net.ops: Globe Telecom, Smart Communications, DITO Telecommunity
net.gb: Prepaid tourist SIM with 5-10GB data typically costs ₱300-500 ($5-9)
net.fwn: SIM cards and load are sold at the airport kiosk on arrival and at Globe/Smart outlets and convenience stores along the main road in town
net.ap: SIM cards and load are sold at the airport kiosk on arrival and at Globe/Smart outlets

tip.s: Tipping isn't obligatory but is increasingly expected and appreciated; ₱20-50 for tricycle drivers, boatmen, and tour guides is customary for good service
tip.r: A 10% service charge is often already added at larger resorts and restaurants; where it isn't, rounding up or leaving about 10% is generous and welcome

pop: General Luna (main hub): 22,853 (2020 census); whole Siargao Island: ~117,000
tagline: Where the waves end and the island wilderness begins
card: Cash is king in Siargao. Most homestays, tricycles, habal-habal drivers, and small eateries are cash-only; only larger resorts and a handful of restaurants in General Luna accept cards. ATMs are limited to a few machines in General Luna and Dapa and can run out of cash on weekends. GCash mobile wallet is widely accepted as a cash alternative.

taxi.color: n/a — no metered taxis exist on the island
taxi.fare: Tricycle in-town: ₱20-30/person day, ₱50/person night; habal-habal short trip (5-10km): ₱50-100; medium (10-30km): ₱100-200; long (30km+): ₱300-400/person
taxi.fareNote: All fares are informally negotiated flat-rate by distance, not metered — agree on price before boarding. Renting a scooter (₱350-600/day) is the most common way solo travelers get around.

emergency.police: 911 (national emergency hotline) or General Luna Municipal Police Station
emergency.medical: Coastal Community Hospital / Lopez General Luna Community Hospital for basic care; serious cases are referred to Surigao City or Cebu
emergency.note: 911 works nationally but response times are slow due to limited island infrastructure. Reef cuts and scooter accidents are the most common tourist injuries — travel insurance with medevac coverage is strongly recommended.

visit: Surf lesson or session at Cloud 9
Explore General Luna town and boardwalk cafes
walk: General Luna's town center and the Cloud 9 boardwalk are walkable/bikeable, but Siargao overall is not a walking destination — attractions are spread across the island, so most visitors rely on rented scooters, habal-habal, or tricycles. Roads outside the main strip can be unpaved, especially after rain.

safety.safety: Generally safe for solo travelers, including women — Siargao has a large, established surfer and digital-nomad community used to visitors. Main risks are road accidents on rented scooters and ocean hazards (reef cuts, rip currents) rather than crime.
safety.crime: Violent crime against tourists is rare. Petty theft from resort rooms and parked bikes does occur — use accommodations with lockers/safes and avoid leaving belongings unattended on beaches.

hood_landmark.Cloud 9: Cloud 9 surf break and wooden watchtower

hood_desc: The island's main tourist hub — General Luna ('GL') is where most restaurants, bars, dive shops, and accommodation cluster along the coastal road leading to the Cloud 9 boardwalk.
The world-famous surf break and its wooden boardwalk over the reef — a compact strip of surf camps, board rentals, and beachfront cafes built right around the wave.
A quieter, greener area just north of Cloud 9, known for the AFAM sunset bridge and rice-paddy backroads, favored by high-end hideaway resorts and long-term nomads.
A remote, uncrowded beach on the northeastern coast, roughly an hour from General Luna over rough roads — popular with surfers seeking less-crowded breaks.
The functional gateway town — home to the ferry port connecting to Surigao City and close to Sayak Airport, with basic lodging and eateries for transiting travelers.

transit.sys: No formal public transit system exists on Siargao
transit.hours: Tricycles and habal-habal generally operate 6am-10pm; night rides cost more and become scarce late
transit.pay: Cash only, paid directly to the driver, fare negotiated up front
transit.map: n/a — no route map; drivers are hailed on the street or arranged via accommodation/Facebook groups
transit.note: Most independent travelers rent their own scooter (₱350-600/day) for flexibility since tricycles don't run fixed routes.

transport.air: Fly into Sayak Airport (IAO), connecting via Cebu (Cebgo, Philippine Airlines, Sunlight Air) or Clark; limited/seasonal direct Manila service.
transport.train: None — no rail service to Mindanao/Siargao
transport.bus: No direct bus to Siargao; buses/vans connect Surigao City to other Mindanao points, then ferry to Dapa
transport.ferry: Fastcraft/RORO ferries run from Surigao City to Dapa port, roughly 3 daily departures, journey 2-4 hours
transport.car: No car rental culture on the island — nearly everyone gets around by rented scooter, habal-habal, or tricycle; some operators offer private van transfers

airport.name: Sayak Airport
airport.distance: ~40 km / 45-60 minutes by road to General Luna and Cloud 9
airport.transport: Shared van (~$5-7, 45-60 min), private van (~$35-45), or pre-arranged hotel transfer

net.m: Good coverage in General Luna and Cloud 9, weaker in remote areas like Pacifico and Sohoton
net.w: Most resorts, cafes, and restaurants in General Luna and Cloud 9 offer free wifi, though speed and reliability vary
net.fwn: Free wifi common at accommodations and cafes in the main tourist strip
net.ap: Local SIM (Globe or Smart) recommended, sold in General Luna town

tip.s: Tipping is not deeply ingrained but increasingly appreciated in the tourism sector — rounding up or leaving 10% at restaurants is welcomed
tip.r: For habal-habal drivers, tour guides, surf instructors, and boat crews, a small tip (₱50-200) is customary and appreciated

tagline: Powder-white sands, dive-worthy reefs, and Bohol's laid-back island soul
card: Larger resorts and restaurants along Alona Beach accept cards, but tricycles, small eateries, and dive shops are often cash-only. ATMs are available around Alona Beach and in Tagbilaran City.

taxi.color: n/a — no metered taxis; tricycles and habal-habal only
taxi.fare: Tricycle short ride: ₱20-50 per person; habal-habal or multicab to Tagbilaran (~12km): ₱100-150
taxi.fareNote: Fares are negotiated/flat-rate; resorts also arrange private van transfers for tours and the airport

emergency.police: 911 (national emergency hotline) or Panglao Municipal Police Station
emergency.medical: Governor Celestino Gallares Memorial Hospital and Ramiro Community Hospital in Tagbilaran City (~20km) are the main referral hospitals
emergency.note: For diving injuries, the nearest hyperbaric chamber is in Cebu City — dive operators carry evacuation protocols. Travel insurance with medevac coverage is recommended.

visit: Sunset walk along the beach strip
Snorkeling and beach time at Alona Beach
Bohol Bee Farm lunch and organic garden tour
Balicasag Island snorkeling/diving with sea turtles
Panglao Church (Our Lady of the Assumption)
walk: Alona Beach's main strip is walkable and packed with restaurants, dive shops, and bars, but Panglao island overall is spread out — reaching Doljo, Momo Beach, or the Bee Farm requires a tricycle, habal-habal, or rented scooter.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers, including women — Panglao is a well-established, resort-driven tourist destination with a strong dive and hospitality community.
safety.crime: Petty theft (unattended valuables on the beach or in unlocked rooms) is the main risk; violent crime against tourists is rare.

hood_landmark.Alona Beach (Tawala): Alona Beach strip and dive shops
hood_landmark.Panglao Poblacion (Town Proper): Our Lady of the Assumption Parish Church

hood_desc: Panglao's busiest tourist strip — a lively stretch of dive shops, beachfront restaurants, massage stalls, and bars right on the white sand, with the widest range of budget-to-mid lodging.
A quieter beach on the island's west side, known for calm, shallow snorkeling reefs and a mellower, less commercial vibe than Alona.
A relaxed stretch of coast anchored by upscale beach resorts and calm swimming waters, popular with couples and families seeking a quieter alternative to Alona.
The municipal center of Panglao, home to the historic Spanish-era church and watchtower, the public market, and everyday local life away from the beach crowds.
A long, wide stretch of white sand favored by resort guests for its calm waters and gentle slope — quieter and more spread out than Alona Beach.

transit.sys: No formal public transit system exists on Panglao
transit.pay: Cash only, fare negotiated or flat-rate up front
transit.map: n/a — no fixed routes; hail tricycles on the street or arrange through your resort
transit.note: Resorts commonly arrange private van transfers for island tours and the airport; renting a scooter is common for independent travelers.

transport.air: Fly into Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG), with direct flights from Manila and Cebu on Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific, and AirAsia
transport.train: None — no rail service in the region
transport.bus: Buses/vans connect Tagbilaran to other Bohol towns and the Chocolate Hills; no direct bus service from Manila
transport.ferry: OceanJet fastcraft from Cebu Pier 1 to Tagbilaran Pier, about 2 hours, multiple daily departures, then a 20-30 minute tricycle or van to Panglao
transport.car: Rental cars and vans available in Tagbilaran; most visitors rely on resort transfers, habal-habal, or a rented scooter

airport.name: Bohol-Panglao International Airport
airport.distance: ~2-7 km from most Panglao resorts (5-15 minutes)
airport.transport: Resort shuttle, tricycle, or private van transfer; no metered taxis

net.m: Good coverage across Panglao from both national carriers
net.w: Most resorts and restaurants along Alona Beach offer free wifi; speeds vary and can slow during peak season
net.fwn: Free wifi common at resorts and restaurants along Alona Beach

tip.s: Tipping is not mandatory but increasingly common at resorts and restaurants — 10% is appreciated where no service charge is included
tip.r: Dive guides, boat crews, and tricycle/habal-habal drivers appreciate a small tip (₱50-150) for good service

tagline: Cobblestones, kalesa bells, and candlelight over Calle Crisologo
card: Cards are accepted at larger hotels and a few upscale restaurants in the heritage core, but most tricycles, kalesa rides, small eateries, and the public market are cash-only. ATMs (BDO, Landbank, Metrobank) cluster around Plaza Salcedo and downtown.

taxi.color: No standardized color scheme — tricycles are independently owned and painted
taxi.fare: ₱15-20 minimum tricycle fare; ₱150-300 for a 30-45 minute kalesa heritage-district tour
taxi.fareNote: Agree on the kalesa fare before boarding — rates are per carriage (up to 3-4 people), not per person; tricycles are unmetered, so confirm price for longer trips

emergency.medical: Gabriela Silang General Hospital (city-run) and Metro Vigan Community Hospital are the two main hospitals serving Vigan
emergency.note: Serious trauma cases are sometimes referred to larger facilities in Laoag or San Fernando; travel insurance is recommended

visit: Padre Burgos House / National Museum branch
walk: Very walkable — the UNESCO heritage core around Calle Crisologo and Plaza Salcedo is compact, flat, and pedestrian-friendly (parts of Calle Crisologo close to vehicles in the evening). Most major sights are within a 15-20 minute walk of each other.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers, including women — Vigan is a small, tourism-oriented heritage city with a strong local police and tourism-police presence around Calle Crisologo and Plaza Salcedo, especially in the evenings.
safety.crime: Petty crime is low; standard precautions apply (watch belongings in the public market, use licensed tricycles at night, agree fares upfront).

hood_landmark.Plaza Salcedo / Downtown Poblacion: Plaza Salcedo dancing fountain and Vigan Cathedral

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed heart of Vigan — ancestral Spanish-Chinese mestizo houses, antique shops, and horse-drawn kalesa clattering over cobblestones.
Vigan's civic and religious core, anchored by the baroque cathedral, the archbishop's palace, and the nightly light-and-water show at Plaza Salcedo.
A working artisan quarter where centuries-old burnay pottery is still hand-thrown and fired in wood-burning kilns.
A quiet hilltop across the Mestizo River famous for its historic bell tower with sweeping views over Vigan and the surrounding rice fields.
The coastal fringe near the airport and Long Beach, offering a low-key seaside break from the heritage-district crowds.

transit.sys: No formal public transit system — tricycles, kalesa, and jeepneys handle local movement; multicabs run longer routes to nearby towns
transit.hours: Roughly 5am-10pm; kalesa mainly operate daytime through early evening
transit.map: No official transit map — routes are informal; ask hotel staff for jeepney routes to outlying barangays
transit.note: Calle Crisologo restricts motor vehicles in the evening, becoming a pedestrian and kalesa-only heritage walk

transport.air: Laoag International Airport (LAO), about 85 km / 1.5-2 hours north, is the main gateway with Cebu Pacific and PAL Express flights from Manila; a small local Vigan Airport has limited regional service
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Vigan or the region
transport.bus: Partas, Farinas Trans, and Dominion operate direct overnight/day buses from Manila to Vigan, roughly 8-9 hours
transport.ferry: No direct passenger ferry service to Vigan
transport.car: Drive via NLEX to TPLEX to the MacArthur Highway/Ilocos coastal roads from Manila, roughly 7-8 hours

airport.name: Laoag International Airport
airport.distance: ~85 km / 1.5-2 hour drive north of Vigan
airport.transport: Van/shuttle transfers, private car hire, or bus connections from Laoag city to Vigan

net.m: Good coverage in Vigan from both national carriers
net.w: Most cafes, restaurants near Calle Crisologo, and hotels offer free wifi
net.ops: Globe Telecom, Smart Communications (including TNT/TM prepaid sub-brands)
net.fwn: Free wifi common at cafes and hotels near the heritage core
net.ap: Prepaid SIMs widely available from local shops

tip.s: Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated — round up or leave 5-10% at restaurants without an existing service charge
tip.r: For kalesa drivers and tricycle rides, a small tip (₱10-20) for good service is a nice gesture, not expected
